messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> P1: GPU OOM spike on pool gpu-pool-us-west-2-3. 30+ OOMs in last 3m, auto-runbook: https://runbook.redwood/gpu-oom. Incident bot attached logs.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: AlertID PD-874321 triggered (pager: oncall-maria). Notifying escalation policy.

oncall-maria: Acked. I'm on it :wave: Starting quick triage. Which customers are hit?

jamal: Seeing repeated `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` from serving runtime on pods in node group `g4-usw2-3`. KV cache eviction rate spiked. Heap traces here:```
2026-06-21T14:15:12Z serving-runtime[pid=4219]: cublas alloc failed: out of memory
GPU 2 - total: 40GB, used: 39.5GB, free: 0.5GB
nvml: GPU 2 mem usage 98%
Stack: runtime/alloc -> kernels/attention -> cublasGemm
```

oncall-maria: Thanks. Are we seeing OOMs on a single model or across multiple model variants?

jamal: Mostly on `redwood/llamax-16k-q4` variant, but also a few hits on `olm/fastgen-13b`. Seems correlated with long-context requests (seq > 8k).

oncall-maria: Customer impact check: hosted-api-us-west-2 5xx rate up ~12% in last 5m. Approx 20 requests/min failing, top customers: acme-retail, datapulse-analytics, few smaller dev orgs. No payment/PII alerts yet.

platform-ops: Noted. Auto-shedder kicked in for pool gpu-pool-us-west-2-3 to prevent total meltdown, but we're still seeing thrash. Autoscaler hasn't added nodes - hitting instance quota in region.

sre-elaine: If quota's the blocker we should reroute traffic to other pools and enable soft-fallback to lower-memory model. Can we do that quickly?

oncall-maria: Plan: (1) cordon and drain the two worst nodes in the pool to force redispatch, (2) update routing policy to fallback -> `llamax-8k-q4` for requests >8k, (3) trigger temporary capacity increase (request via cloud console) and (4) if OOMs continue, restart serving-runtime on affected pods. Doing 1 & 2 now.

jamal: Doing drain on node g4-usw2-3-node-07:```sh
kubectl cordon g4-usw2-3-node-07
kubectl drain g4-usw2-3-node-07 --force --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30
```

oncall-maria: Routing change applied: fallback rule updated for route `/v1/generate` in us-west-2 to prefer `llamax-8k-q4` for long seqs. Propagating. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: Escalation: if not resolved in 15m, pager will escalate to secondary oncall. Timer started.

jamal: After drain, observed ephemeral drop in OOMs but then another spike on different node (g4-usw2-3-node-03). Looks like fragmentation + large-prefix KV cache growth. Heap snapshots show many active KV entries for repeated long-prefix prompts.

oncall-maria: Quick mitigation: reduce KV cache retention to 60s for that pool and enable prefix trimming. Patching config:```json
{"pool":"gpu-pool-us-west-2-3","kv_cache": {"enabled": true, "retention_seconds": 60, "trim_threshold_mb": 512}}
```
Applying now.

platform-ops: Patch applied to pool. Rolling restart of serving runtime pods in pool scheduled.

jamal: Logs after patch: `kv_cache: trimming 1.2GB entries -> freed 1.05GB` then `serving-runtime: recovered 120MB free on GPU 2` Good signal but still jittery.

oncall-maria: Customer impact update: 5xx rate down to ~4% after routing fallback and cache trim. We mitigated immediate customer-facing failures. Notifying customers via status page.

sre-elaine: Nice work. Please escalate to infra to request quota increase -> region us-west-2 GPU quota +10. Also we should run a postmortem if this recurs.

platform-ops: Quota request raised with cloud support (case #CS-342198). ETA 2h but trying for expedited approval.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Manual escalation triggered to secondary (oncall-kevin) due to sustained alerts.

oncall-maria: Handing off to kevin for follow-up & post-incident ops (I'm at end of shift). Summary: P1 GPU OOM spike on gpu-pool-us-west-2-3 driven by high long-context KV cache usage for llamax-16k; mitigations applied: node drains x2, routing fallback to llamax-8k, KV cache retention reduced, rolling restart of runtime pods. Customer-impact: transient 5xx up to 12% peak, now ~4%, major customers were affected but recovered. Runbook: https://runbook.redwood/gpu-oom — follow steps 4-7 for postmortem.

oncall-kevin: Acked handoff :+1: I'll take over. Will keep the pager on and monitor for 30m, then coordinate postmortem if stable. Can you drop any debug captures (heap dumps/log bundles) in #incident-artifacts?

oncall-maria: Dropping logs to incident-artifacts now: `/artifacts/PD-874321/` - includes heap snapshots, nvml snapshots, and `kubectl describe` outputs.

oncall-kevin: Got them. First priority: ensure autoscaler doesn't re-add jobs to same fragmenting nodes; second: confirm KV trimming prevents recurrence for 60m. If we see >5 OOMs in next 15m -> escalate to SRE infra for emergency node replacement.

sre-elaine: I'll be on standby. If necessary we can failover the pool entirely to fallback pool in a maintenance window.

oncall-kevin: Thanks. Marking as "mitigated but monitoring" and leaving PD alert open until stable.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Alert PD-874321 acknowledged by oncall-maria, reassigned to oncall-kevin.

oncall-kevin: final note for now: no customer data exposure, no credentials involved, root cause suspected memory blowup from unbounded KV entries on long-context workloads. Postmortem owner needed: assigning jamal.

jamal: Happy to own postmortem. Will collect reproducible prompt set + `kv-cache` metric export and propose long-term fixes (bounded kv entries per request, preemptive eviction heuristics).

oncall-kevin: Thanks team. Keeping channel open for updates. :lock:
